The Chirps and the Welcome Tree

The Day the Welcomes Flew

At last it was Everybody Day. The paper leaves on the Welcome Tree rustled outside the crooked-roof birdhouse. Bella straightened one. Chip straightened another. Daisy straightened Chip. Caty opened the gate.

Mouse arrived with his family. Moth brought her cousins. Toad arrived in a hat that looked suspiciously like lunch. Bella took a breath to say welcome. The wind took a bigger breath. WHOOF!

Leaves went over the fence. Leaves went into the hedge. One got stuck to Daisy’s crest. The Welcome Tree stood bare. “They’ve only just arrived,” Chip whispered. “How will anybody know what to do?”

Bella ran after the leaf with three bumpy stones on it. Mouse had caught it. He showed it to his cousins and led them along the path to the turn. Bella stopped running. The picture was doing its job.

Across the grass Moth found the leaf with a seat and a little doorstep. She invited a tired traveler to rest. Beetle caught the drum leaf, the one with a gap in the pattern. A small paw tapped a beat right in the gap.

“Leave the leaves with the finders!” Bella called. “The welcomes can walk!” Daisy held the gate wide. Chip showed a guest the way in. Caty held out a crayon. Soon guests were welcoming other guests.

A little wren stood at the bare branch. “Have I missed it all?” she asked. Bella gave her a blank leaf. “What would you like to bring?” Wren drew a round egg with a crack down the middle. “Riddles,” she said.

That evening they hung the pictures back wherever a twig felt right. Wren’s riddle rustled beside Daisy’s picture of a bare branch. Bella left one twig empty. From the gate came a tiny voice. “Is there room?” Bella hopped down. “I saved you a leaf.”

Read together

What would you put on a blank leaf for the next visitor?
